caption: Forty days into my Money Rhythm streak and it's the reason I caught the school fees jump before the debit order did. What would catch you out this month?

Living in Stellenbosch
slides.body:
Female, 36
Married, two kids (6 and 9)
Job: Hospitality manager, wine estate
Net salary: R29 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond contribution
slides.includes: Our share of the family home bond
slides.body: We split it roughly by income. This is my half.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family of four, big monthly shop plus the school lunch top-ups
slides.body: Two growing kids. This number only moves one way.

slides.title: School fees & aftercare
slides.includes: Fees for both kids, aftercare for the younger one
slides.body: Aftercare isn't optional when my shifts run past five most days.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: The most boring line on this list and the one I never think about.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Family plan, upgraded when our youngest started school
slides.body: Worth it every time someone comes home with a note from the school nurse.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol, phone & fibre, funeral policies, a stokvel with the estate staff, black tax to my side of the family, savings
slides.body: Eight thousand nine hundred rand of things I'd never once tracked in one place before this year.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R29 000. Forty days into checking in on Money Rhythm every morning, and this is the first month I've actually seen this number coming.

slides.title: I stopped being surprised by my own month
slides.body:
Forty days into a daily check-in streak on Beyond Horizon's Money Rhythm, and it's the first time I've noticed a bill creeping up before the debit order hit.

The school fees jump was one I caught three days early instead of finding out on payday.

No bank login needed.
